purpose: Define the meaning and direction of responses before assigning numeric scoring weights.
critical_constraint: Do not convert response bands directly into assumed weights until historical regression tests and evidence review have been used to calibrate them.

historical_model.response_model: The current SuperForms configuration uses Yes=1 and No=0 and direct sums for the nine body-system calculators.
historical_model.2026_change: The proposed questionnaire will support ordinal and categorical responses, so scoring must become response-aware rather than treating every non-zero answer as equivalent.

scoring_layers.purpose: Age range, gender/applicability and dietary preferences/restrictions.
scoring_layers.scoring: Filtering/applicability and recommendation context; does not independently create a physiological need.

scoring_layers.purpose: Food allergy, medication/medical supervision and clinically sensitive symptoms.
scoring_layers.scoring: Flags, exclusions or cautions; normally no positive/negative wellness score.

scoring_layers.purpose: Smoking, alcohol, caffeine, red/processed meat, air pollution, sedentary behaviour, UPF and similar behaviours.
scoring_layers.scoring: Potentially ordinal exposure signal, with direction and magnitude evidence-calibrated.

scoring_layers.purpose: Sleep, digestive discomfort, pain, worry, fatigue and similar self-reported experiences.
scoring_layers.scoring: Frequency/severity indicates signal strength but does not establish diagnosis or cause.

scoring_layers.purpose: What the person wants to improve.
scoring_layers.scoring: Prioritises outcomes; does not manufacture a body-system deficit.

response_rules.rule: Higher-frequency/severity responses generally produce stronger signals where a monotonic relationship is evidence-supported.
Higher exposure may produce stronger relevance signals where supported by evidence; do not assume linearity or universal thresholds.
Distinct categories should map to distinct rules rather than automatically becoming 0/1.
Selected items may create separate signals, but closely related selections must not be double-counted.
Not applicable must be distinct from No/None, especially for sex-specific questions.

proposed_calibration_sequence: Finalise question constructs and response options.
Map each response to evidence-backed signals.
Assign provisional direction only before assigning numeric magnitude.
Compare proposed mappings with historical question-to-system mappings.
Use the 19 usable scored historical records as regression tests; exclude the record without nine-system scores.
Introduce numeric weights only where evidence and model behaviour justify them.
Validate score distributions, question sensitivity and outcome ranking.
validation_warning: The existing validation shows systematic mismatches between recorded historical scores and simple question-to-system Yes/No sums, especially for Glandular, Respiratory and Urinary. The old direct-sum model therefore should not be assumed to be the complete authoritative specification.
